details:
What is the ATLTEC project?

ATLTEC is an intelligent, autonomous system designed to generate water from atmospheric humidity and automate precision agriculture in semi-arid regions, such as Tlayecac, Ayala, Morelos. Its architecture combines open-source hardware (ESP32) with edge intelligence (TinyML) and geospatial telemetry. By leveraging data from NASA satellites, the system delivers exceptional performance for farmers, helping to protect and save crops—and, by extension, entire local economies.

1. Geothermal and Condensation System

• PVC Pipe Intake: A microcontroller-controlled fan draws moisture-laden ambient air into the main system.

• Geothermal Cooling (Buried Copper Piping): The air passes through copper pipes installed vertically and horizontally underground. Due to the earth's thermal inertia, the pipes remain cooler than the outside air, triggering a natural thermal shock (reaching the dew point) without the need for expensive electric compressors.

• Collection and Irrigation: The condensed water drips into a collection reservoir, from which an automated solenoid valve and pump distribute the water directly to the roots of the crops (such as lemon trees).

2. Local Sensors and Intelligence (TinyML)

The system employs local sensors (such as the DHT11, AHT20, and the LM393 soil moisture sensor) connected to an ESP32 microcontroller. Using integrated logic thresholds, the system continuously evaluates whether environmental conditions are suitable for water generation:

• When relative humidity reaches between 45% and 65%, the fan and system components activate (enabling optimal water generation). • If the environment is too dry, the fan shuts off automatically to avoid unnecessary consumption of solar or battery power when condensation is not feasible.

3. Integration with the NASA POWER API

Through the official NASA API (https://power.larc.nasa.gov/parameters/), ATLTEC retrieves macroclimatic parameters for the precise geolocation of Tlayecac (Lat: 18.75, Lon: -98.8833), including:

• T2M & RH2M: Temperature and Relative Humidity at 2 meters.

• PRECTOTCORR: Corrected precipitation data for estimating potential rainfall.

• ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN: Surface solar radiation, used to calculate evapotranspiration cycles.

4. Planting Decisions, Climate, and Viability in Morelos

By cross-referencing local and satellite data, the platform determines:

• Planting Feasibility: It evaluates soil water stress and ambient temperature to indicate whether conditions are favorable for germination.

• Irrigation Optimization: It activates the water pump only when soil moisture falls below the levels optimal for the specific crop.

• Water Generation in Morelos (Upcoming Months): It identifies optimal microclimates within the state. While warm, low-lying areas (such as Yautepec) require constant, technical irrigation, forested areas or regions with humid microclimates (such as Tepoztlán or the higher-altitude parts of Ayala and Huitzililla) offer high potential for atmospheric water harvesting for much of the year.

5. Dew Point Calculation, Water Generation, and Rainfall Forecasting

The analytical core of ATLTEC combines satellite data from NASA POWER with real-time measurements from local sensors to drive automated decision-making:

• Dew Point Calculation: By combining ambient temperature and relative humidity (sourced from NASA and cross-referenced with data from DHT11/AHT20 sensors), the system precisely calculates the temperature at which invisible water vapor in the air condenses into liquid. We know exactly when the buried copper pipe will reach the necessary natural thermal differential.

• When Can Water Be Generated?: The system autonomously determines the optimal time for operation. If the relative humidity is high and the dew point is favorable, the fan is activated. If the air is too dry (humidity below a critical threshold), the system suspends operation to save energy.

• When to sow?: By cross-referencing soil temperature, humidity levels measured by the sensor, and NASA solar radiation indices, the platform determines whether the soil’s moisture status is appropriate to ensure seed germination without the risk of premature drought.

• Rainfall Detection and Forecasting: Using NASA’s corrected precipitation parameter (PRECTOTCORR) and monitoring for sudden drops in barometric pressure alongside spikes in humidity, the system anticipates rainfall, allowing it to pause automated irrigation to prevent waterlogging of the crops.

This supports agricultural sustainability and economic stability. Acknowledging that water scarcity is a pressing issue, our system—which recovers and manages water within controlled environments—promotes significant water conservation. Although ATLTEC is currently designed for greenhouses or small plots, the project is fully scalable.

Our platform is currently being piloted in Morelos, where we compare local data with satellite information. This allows for accurate visualization, helping to prevent errors in planning planting seasons or crop rotation, while also improving water collection and management.

It is worth noting that our initiative began after a friend and her family lost most of their crops due to unpredictable rainfall—it failed to rain when it was expected to, resulting in losses for her family and food shortages in their community. This experience highlighted the vital importance of having precise data in agriculture. Born out of that difficult situation, our goal is to prevent—and, where possible, eliminate—the losses and negative impacts caused by climate change, water scarcity, and uncontrollable factors like erratic rainfall, ensuring that other farmers do not have to face similar hardships.
